correctness.rationale: Assessment of /workspace/repairs/4/RESULT.md. The cup-length theorem in the original survives for every lattice, but the original line 19 also asserted the rational-ring identification for the fixed graphical rational presentation, which is false in that generality. For two disjoint edges the real Lie group is a product of two real Heisenberg groups. It has the lattice of Heisenberg matrices with entries in Z[sqrt(2)], embedded via the two real embeddings: the integer ring embeds as a full lattice under these embeddings, and the abelian coordinates and then the center admit bounded fundamental sets. In the rational H¹ basis x1,x2,y1,y2 dual to coefficients of 1 and sqrt(2) in the abelian coordinates, the kernel of the degree-one wedge-to-cup map is spanned by f=x1∧y1+2x2∧y2 and g=x1∧y2+x2∧y1, by multiplication in Q(sqrt(2)). These are exactly the two degree-two boundaries on degree-one classes, seen over R by the invariant model and then descended in the rational H¹ basis. No nonzero p f+q g is decomposable over Q, since its square vanishes only if q²=2p². The split graphical rational model has a decomposable nonzero kernel element from either edge. Thus the two rational rings cannot be isomorphic. The replacement restricts the invariant-form comparison and displayed factors to R; it obtains rational cup-length and a rational top product by scalar extension, not by choosing rational invariant vertex forms. Independently verified the proof after that change: every differential target from a pure-edge monomial identifies the removed edge by its unique vertex pair and reconstructs the source monomial; terms from the vertex ideal have at least three vertex factors and cannot cancel it. Hence every positive-degree cocycle is in the vertex ideal, which has zero (n+1)st power. Allocating each edge to one endpoint makes each of the n factors closed by repeated vertex generators; the product is the full volume monomial and cannot be a boundary, since differentiation removes an edge. The proof includes isolated vertices and the edgeless graph. Nomizu gives the real ring for any lattice. Expanding the real top product in rational bases in the same factor degrees produces a nonzero rational product in top degree; faithfulness of scalar extension gives the upper bound. No bundled program execution or formal verification is claimed.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem gives an exact, natural multiplicative invariant for an entire standard family without computing the cohomology ring. Independence from the edge set is nontrivial because each new edge changes the dimension and differential. A concrete factorization of the top class and a vanishing bound at n+1 distinguish it from mere additive cohomology or a dimension estimate. The correction retains every lattice and both coefficient fields while removing an incorrect auxiliary ring claim.
